question: An investigator is studying the structural integrity of collagen. Human fibroblasts are cultured on a medium and different enzymes are applied. One of the cultures is supplemented with an enzyme that inhibits the formation of hydrogen and disulfide bonds between collagen α-chains. Which of the following processes is most likely to be impaired as a result?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Inhibition of hydrogen and disulfide bond formation in collagen -> Impaired collagen stability -> Impaired bone matrix synthesis -> 80% CHAIN: Inhibition of collagen α-chain bonding -> Impaired ligament relaxation -> 70% CHAIN: Disruption of collagen α-chain bonds -> Impaired osteoclast activation -> 60% CHAIN: Enzyme inhibition affecting collagen α-chain bonds -> Impaired internal elastic lamina formation -> 70% CHAIN: Interference with collagen α-chain bonding -> Impaired cartilaginous growth plate mineralization -> 80%
analysis: The enzyme inhibiting the formation of hydrogen and disulfide bonds between collagen α-chains would impair the structural integrity of collagen. Since collagen is a major component of bone matrix, the most likely process to be impaired as a result would be bone matrix synthesis.
